result.title: Neural Agent Compiler: Learning to Schedule Soft Dependencies
result.summary: Large language model agents accomplish complex tasks by coordinating multiple reasoning steps and tool operations, which form dependencies among their operations. Existing orchestration methods primarily consider hard dependencies that determine when an operation can legally begin, but overlook soft dependencies, i.e., information that is not required for execution but may improve an already executable operation. We identify soft-dependency scheduling as an important problem in agent execution. To this end, we introduce Neural Agent Compiler (NAC), a learned scheduler that predicts the task-quality and resource consequences of three execution modes and selects the highest-utility legal mode at a scheduling boundary. NAC represents the executable continuation, pending information event, and resource state in a shared memory, and uses a utility function to adapt the consequence predictions to different resource preferences. Across AppWorld, WebShop, and $τ^2$-bench, NAC achieves 276/417 AppWorld task completions, a 74.69 WebShop Task Score, and 59/100 $τ^2$-bench successes. Additional studies show that the learned scheduler reduces execution work, establishing soft-dependency scheduling as a promising solution for orchestrating tool-using agents.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Neural Agent Compiler，一个可学习的 agent 调度器：在调度边界上预测「立即继续执行」「等待未到达信息」「受资源约束」三种模式对任务质量和资源消耗的后果，用效用函数按资源偏好选择最优合法模式，并在 AppWorld、WebShop、τ²-bench 上验证其减少执行开销。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把「是否等待额外信息」与直接执行的收益—成本纳入同一效用预测，可能为 LVR 的 THINK/LOOK/STOP 决策与停止成本提供可核查的建模线索，但对象是纯文本工具 agent、不涉及视觉状态，迁移性待判断。
